passage:
I'm Kalyani, and I work at the toy shop in the market. On Saturday a little boy, Arnab, came in with his grandfather, who told him, "Pick any one toy."
Arnab walked down our long aisle of cars, dolls, puzzles and balls. He picked up a truck, put it down, touched a drum. Then he stood in the middle and started to cry. I can't say what he was thinking.
His grandfather knelt and held up just two things: a red truck and a small drum. "This or this?"
Arnab grabbed the truck and hugged it all the way to the counter.

qa.q: What two toys did Arnab's grandfather hold up?
qa.a: A red truck and a small drum.

qa.q: Why might Arnab have started to cry in the middle of the aisle?
qa.a: With so many cars, dolls, puzzles and balls, every choice may have felt too big, and not knowing which one to pick could have upset him. 😢

qa.q: Which choice by the grandfather turned things around, and why?
qa.a: Holding up just two toys, because a small choice was easy for Arnab to make and he could feel happy with it.

qa.q: How does Kalyani see the scene?
qa.a: Kalyani watches from the shop, sees the crying and then the happy hug, and admits not knowing what Arnab was thinking.

grounding: A shop worker describes a young child who is overwhelmed by a long aisle of toys but chooses happily from two.

passage:
Saturday: At the big toy fair, Zainab's aunt Aditi said, "Choose one!" Zainab stared at walls of toys, touched ten things, then sat on the floor and cried. They left with nothing.
Tuesday: At home, Aditi put just three things on the bed: a ball, a puzzle, a doll. "Which one for today?" Zainab picked the puzzle at once and did it twice.
The next Saturday: At a tiny toy shop near the mosque, Aditi asked the shopkeeper to show three small toys only. Zainab looked, chose the wooden bird, and skipped out holding it high.

qa.q: What did Zainab choose at the tiny toy shop?
qa.a: Zainab chose the wooden bird.

qa.q: What was Zainab feeling at the big toy fair, and what shows it?
qa.a: Zainab seemed overwhelmed and upset; she touched ten things, then sat on the floor and cried.

qa.q: What was Aditi's turning point, and why did it help?
qa.a: On Tuesday Aditi offered only three things, which let Zainab choose easily, so she used the same idea at the shop.

qa.q: What might Aditi have felt leaving the toy fair with nothing?
qa.a: Aditi may have felt puzzled and a bit sad, since she meant the big choice as a treat and it ended in tears.

grounding: Shows over a week how a young child freezes before too many toys but chooses happily from three.

passage:
The toy shop in the mall was closing in ten minutes, and Indu had only two hundred rupees left for her son's birthday gift. "Anything from this wall, Vaibhav," she said.
The wall was huge: cars, robots, bubble guns, puzzles, balls. Vaibhav reached for a robot, then a car, then a ball, and froze, his lip trembling. The lights started switching off at the back. "Quick, quick," Indu said.
Vaibhav began to wail and grabbed the nearest thing, a plastic whistle.
At home he blew it once and dropped it. Next time, Indu thought, she'd pick three toys and let him choose.

qa.q: What did Vaibhav grab in the end?
qa.a: Vaibhav grabbed the nearest thing, a plastic whistle.

qa.q: Why did Vaibhav freeze in front of the wall?
qa.a: So many cars, robots and balls, plus the rush, made each choice feel uncertain, and he couldn't settle on one.

qa.q: What plan does Indu make, and why is it likely to work?
qa.a: She plans to pick three toys and let him choose, because a small set is easier for a young child and he may enjoy what he picks.

qa.q: What was the rush like for Indu?
qa.a: Indu had little money and ten minutes, and her 'Quick, quick' shows how stressed she was as the lights went off.

grounding: Shows a young child who, facing a huge wall of toys under time pressure, freezes, cries and grabs the nearest item.

passage: Seema Masi took Leela to the new toy shop near their Pune colony. "Choose anything you like!" The shelves went up to the ceiling: dolls, trains, kites, clay, puzzles, drums. Leela picked up a kite, put it back, touched a train, looked at the dolls. Her lip began to wobble. She grabbed the rubber ball nearest the counter and held it tight. At home she pushed it under the sofa. The next week Masi put just three things on the mat: clay, a puzzle and a kite. Leela chose the clay and made snakes all evening.

qa.q: What did Leela grab in the toy shop?
qa.a: The rubber ball nearest the counter.

qa.q: What does Leela's wobbling lip suggest she was feeling in the big shop?
qa.a: It suggests she felt overwhelmed and upset, because every toy looked possible and she couldn't settle on one 😢

qa.q: What did Seema Masi change the next week, and why did it work?
qa.a: She put just three things on the mat, so choosing felt easy and Leela was happy with the clay all evening.

qa.q: What might Seema Masi have felt when Leela pushed the ball under the sofa?
qa.a: She may have felt puzzled or a little disappointed, since she had offered anything at all and Leela still didn't enjoy her pick.

grounding: A young child faced with shelves of toys freezes, nearly cries and grabs the nearest one, but enjoys choosing from three.

passage:
"Papa, I want... that one. No, that one!" Chaitanya's finger jumped from robot to truck to drum.
"Take your time," said Lalit, his father.
"There's too much!" Chaitanya sat down on the shop floor, eyes wet.
Lalit crouched beside him. "Okay. Let's make it small. Close your eyes." He took three toys off the shelf: a red truck, a drum and a robot. "Open. Only these three."
Chaitanya looked. He touched the truck. "This one."
"Sure?"
"Yes! Vroom!" He zoomed it along Papa's knee, all the way to the counter.

qa.q: Which three toys did Lalit take off the shelf?
qa.a: A red truck, a drum and a robot.

qa.q: What does Chaitanya sitting on the floor with wet eyes suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: He felt swamped and frustrated, because there were too many toys and he couldn't pick one.

qa.q: What choice did Lalit make that turned things around?
qa.a: Instead of hurrying him or leaving, he cut the choice down to three toys, which made picking quick and left Chaitanya happy with the truck.

qa.q: What might that moment on the shop floor have been like for Lalit?
qa.a: He may have felt a mix of worry and patience, wanting his son to enjoy the treat rather than end it in tears.

grounding: A father sees his young son freeze and cry among too many toys and makes choosing easy by offering only three.
